lines: A four-foot beetle with hardened wing covers and chewing mandibles.

sections.title: Special attacks and defenses mechanics
lines: Acid cloud · When attacked or disturbed, it has a 50% chance each round to turn and discharge an 8-foot sphere of reddish acidic vapor from its abdomen. The cloud deals 3d4 damage per round to a creature within it. It can discharge every third round and at most twice in eight hours.

Sound of the discharge · Within 15 feet, creatures that can hear have a 20% chance of being stunned. A creature that avoids the stun has a separate 20% chance of deafness. Stun lasts 2d4 rounds followed by 2d4 rounds of deafness. Deafness alone lasts 2d6 rounds.
Printed defense · The table lists fire cloud as a separate special defense. The text describes the acidic discharge and gives no separate procedure for a fire cloud.

Rotting wood and underground tunnels

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A nine-foot burrowing beetle with large chewing mandibles.

sections.title: Habitat and behavior mechanics
lines: Rotting wood · The beetle feeds on rotting wood and similar matter. It is found alone in large trees and can gather in underground tunnel complexes.
Fungus farms · Tunnel colonies cultivate fungi for food. They react quickly when shriekers in the farm sound an alarm.
Reported nest intelligence · The account describes rumors of nests that reason collectively at a human level. An individual beetle has Animal intelligence (1).

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A beetle with two small red-glowing glands above its eyes and another near the back of its abdomen.

sections.title: Traits mechanics
lines: Cold light · Three glands shed cool red light in a 10-foot radius. The light persists for 1d6 days after removal.
Mandibles · The beetle attacks with its mandibles for the table’s 2–8 damage. The glowing glands produce no heat.

siblings.description: A giant fire beetle is a nocturnal creature that takes its name from a pair of glowing glands that give off light. Miners and adventurers prize these creatures, for a giant fire beetle’s glands continue to shed light for 1d6 days after the beetle dies. Giant fire beetles are most commonly found underground and in dark forests.
